title: The values of rational probabilistic finite automata are the left-c.e. reals
description: Which real numbers are values of probabilistic finite automata with rational transition probabilities and rational initial distributions? We prove that they are exactly the left-c.e. reals in [0,1], the limits of computable nondecreasing rational sequences, and that two input letters and one fixed number of states suffice. The value is the supremum of acceptance probabilities over finite words. It was known that the value cannot be computed or approximated from the automaton; here a single automaton has a noncomputable value, given explicitly relative to a fixed enumeration of Turing machines. The construction checks counter-machine histories by a likelihood test in the manner of Condon and Lipton and pays a reward read from the output. It is effective given a rational interval around the target, but cannot be made effective from its approximations alone. Every prefix-free halting probability, including Chaitin's Ω, is a value. A construction of Elkouss and Pérez-García also realizes every left-c.e. real in [0,1] as a rational finite-state channel capacity. For quantum automata with algebraic data, measure-once values are algebraic, while rational quantum channels and QFAs with control language realize all left-c.e. reals in [0,1]; computability for one-way Kondacs–Watrous measure-many automata remains open.
notes: Preprint. It has not been peer reviewed. Version 1.1.0. Version 1.1.0 adds Section 9, "Quantum automata: where the ladder breaks": measure-once quantum automata with algebraic data have algebraic values (implicit in Derksen, Jeandel and Koiran); automata whose letters act by rational quantum channels, and quantum automata with control language, have exactly the left-c.e. reals in [0,1] as values; computability of the values of one-way Kondacs-Watrous measure-many automata is posed as an open question, and two subclasses of that model are proved to have computable values. A two-way extension is deferred to version 1.2 (proof in preparation). The former Section 9 is now Section 10 (Corollary 9.7 is now Corollary 10.7). The abstract is shortened, five references are added, and an exact checker for the control-language and channel constructions, paper/quantum_checks.py, ships with its recorded output; no proof depends on it. Theorems A-D and their proofs are unchanged. Version 1.0.2 corrected the version string on the title page of the PDF.
